speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, and welcome back to The Cognitive Revolution.
zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 The Cognitive Revolution。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, I'm excited to welcome Kirthana Gopalakrishnan, staff research scientist at Google DeepMind and research lead for Gemini Robotics, back for her fourth annual appearance on the show.
zh: 今天，我很高兴欢迎 Google DeepMind 资深研究科学家、Gemini Robotics 研究负责人 Kirthana Gopalakrishnan 第四次做客本节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the biggest questions in AI today is how soon will general purpose robots become broadly useful?
zh: 如今 AI 领域最大的问题之一是：通用机器人还需要多久才能变得广泛有用？

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is already affecting the world in major ways, even in its purely digital form.
zh: 即使处于纯数字形态，AI 已经在以重大的方式影响着世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the most sci-fi forecasts for the AI future predict that robotics will soon hit key tipping points.
zh: 但对 AI 未来最科幻的预测认为，机器人技术即将迎来关键的转折点。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI-2027, for example, predicts that humanoid robots will become useful sometime in mid-2027, and that by 2028, a whole robot economy could take shape, where robots build more robot factories, which in turn produce more robots, leading to unprecedented exponential economic growth, but also creating serious risk of AI takeover.
zh: 例如，AI-2027 预测人形机器人将在 2027 年年中某个时候变得有用，而到 2028 年，一个完整的机器人经济可能会形成——机器人建造更多的机器人工厂，这些工厂又生产更多的机器人，从而带来前所未有的指数级经济增长，但同时也带来 AI 接管的严重风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, how does that vision line up with the reality of robotics research today?
zh: 那么，这一愿景与当今机器人技术研究的现实相比如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: We begin with a discussion of the extremely viral Robot Olympics held in China this summer, as I was really curious to get Kirtan's take on what it means that humanoid robots can now run faster than the fastest humans.
zh: 我们从对今年夏天在中国举行的、极其火爆的机器人奥运会的讨论开始，因为我很好奇 Kirtana 对此的看法——即人形机器人现在能跑得比最快的人类还快，这意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Her point of view, as you'll hear, inverts the usual US-China dichotomy in AI.
zh: 正如你将听到的，她的观点颠覆了 AI 领域通常的中美二元对立叙事。

speaker: Unknown
en: She says that while the videos are obviously impressive, skills like running on a flat track are actually relatively easy to train in simulation.
zh: 她说，虽然那些视频显然令人印象深刻，但在平坦跑道上奔跑这类技能实际上在模拟中是相对容易训练的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And more to the point, foot speed is not really a limiting factor in the utility that robots can provide.
zh: 更关键的是，奔跑速度并不是机器人所能提供的实用性中真正的限制因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: As such, her team at Google is more focused on practical value.
zh: 因此，她在 Google 的团队更关注实际价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: From there, we get into Gemini Robotics 2, a suite of three models that Google released this summer.
zh: 接下来，我们谈到了 Gemini Robotics 2，这是 Google 今年夏天发布的一套三个模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gemini Robotics ER 2, for embodied reasoning, which Kirthina describes as a System 2 for robotics control, is based on Gemini Flash and is available via the API, allowing developers to define the affordances available to the models as tools just like we do with digital agents.
zh: Gemini Robotics ER 2,用于具身推理，Kirthina 将其描述为机器人控制的 System 2，它基于 Gemini Flash，可通过 API 获取，允许开发者将模型可用的可供性定义为工具，就像我们对数字智能体所做的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I played around with it and found it remarkably accessible.
zh: 我上手试了一下，发现它非常容易上手。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other two models, Gemini Robotics 2 and Gemini Robotics On-Device 2, translate these higher-level tool calls down to the level of robot action and are now capable of controlling the whole robot from fingertips to feet on a wide range of form factors, but are currently available only to trusted testers.
zh: 另外两个模型，Gemini Robotics 2 和 Gemini Robotics On-Device 2，将这些更高层次的工具调用转化到机器人动作层面，现在已能控制从指尖到脚部的整个机器人在广泛的本体形态上，但目前仅向受信任的测试者开放。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having understood how these models work, we again zoom out, and I ask Kirtana how she understands progress in robotics overall.
zh: 在理解了这些模型的工作原理之后，我们再次拉远视角，我问 Kirtana 她如何理解机器人技术的整体进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the one hand, like so many other AI researchers recently, she says that she has been surprised by the pace of progress.
zh: 一方面，像最近许多其他 AI 研究者一样，她说她对进展的速度感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the same time, she still feels that robotics remains in its GPT-2 era.
zh: 但与此同时，她仍然认为机器人技术仍处于其 GPT-2 时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have seen a number of recent demos of robots learning new tasks from just a few or even just a single human demonstration.
zh: 我们已经看到许多最近的演示，机器人仅从少数甚至单次人类演示中学习新任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: But Kierthen argues that the range of tasks you can teach this way and the generalization profile of robotics models across different robot bodies still isn't strong enough to deliver the versatility and reliability that real-world use cases demand.
zh: 但 Kierthen 认为，你可以用这种方式教给机器人的任务范围，以及机器人模型在不同机器人本体之间的泛化能力，仍然不够强大，无法提供真实世界用例所需的多功能性和可靠性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Toward the end, we move on to talk about recent progress in hardware, where robots are likely to be deployed at scale first, whether capabilities or safety, alignment, and robustness will ultimately be the limiting factor for the consumer market, and we consider the future of the field.
zh: 接近尾声时，我们转向谈论硬件方面的最新进展，机器人最有可能首先在哪里大规模部署，能力还是安全性、对齐和鲁棒性最终会成为消费市场的限制因素，我们还展望了这个领域的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Including whether we can continue to run LLM-derived robotics models in a loop, as today's systems mostly do, or we'll need some sort of predictive world modeling, as we humans use, to create systems that can anticipate and smoothly interact with the world.
zh: 包括我们是否可以继续像今天的系统大多所做的那样，让基于 LLM 的机器人模型循环运行，还是我们需要某种预测性的世界建模——就像我们人类所使用的——来创建能够预判并与世界流畅交互的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: On that question, and on the timeline for key utility milestones, Kirtana isn't one to speculate too wildly.
zh: 对于那个问题，以及关键实用性里程碑的时间线，Kirtana 不是一个会过度投机的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: For her, these are all empirical questions to be resolved by research and experimentation.
zh: 对她来说，这些都是需要通过研究和实验来解决的经验性问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what is clear to me coming out of this conversation is that robotics will either need to hit key tipping points soon, or some of the most aggressive timelines for AI transformation will have to be pushed back.
zh: 但从这次对话中让我清楚的是，机器人技术要么需要很快迎来关键转折点，否则一些最激进的 AI 变革时间线将不得不被推迟。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that, I hope you enjoy this very well-grounded update on the state of robotics with Kirthana Gopalakrishnan from Google DeepMind.
zh: 话就说到这里，希望你喜欢这次来自 Google DeepMind 的 Kirthana Gopalakrishnan 关于机器人技术现状的、非常脚踏实地的更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, it has been very useful in having an expert go over your problems where you're probably not very skilled to solve.
zh: 是的，让一个专家来过一遍你不擅长解决的问题，这非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I'm a big voice mode fan too, actually.
zh: 是的，其实我也是语音模式的忠实粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a previous conversation that we had, I asked you what you most needed from hardware makers, and you said, I need good hands.
zh: 在我们之前的一次对话中，我问你最需要硬件制造商提供什么，你说，我需要好的手。

speaker: Unknown
en: How are hands coming along?
zh: 手的进展怎么样了？

speaker: Unknown
en: How is hardware coming along generally?
zh: 硬件总体上进展如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you pleased with the progress?
zh: 你对进展满意吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it going to become a bottleneck for you relative to how fast the models are improving?
zh: 相对于模型改进的速度，它会成为你的瓶颈吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do we stand?
zh: 我们现在处于什么阶段？

speaker: Unknown
en: When I last spoke to you was probably in the May, March of last year, right?
zh: 我上次和你聊大概是在去年五月、三月，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's the interesting thing, right?
zh: 那么有意思的事情来了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We had in the March of last year, we came up with Gemini Robotics 1, which showed that a lot of dexterity with grippers.
zh: 我们在去年三月推出了 Gemini Robotics 1，它展示了用夹爪实现的大量灵巧性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the summer of this year, and it's only like a year and four, four months, right?
zh: 而在今年夏天，也就是只过了大概一年零四，四个月，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Three months, a year and a quarter.
zh: 三个月，一年零一个季度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We showed Gemini Robotics 2, which does multifinger dexterity, which can tie trash bags and stuff and do very fine control of multifingered hands.
zh: 我们展示了 Gemini Robotics 2，它能做多手指灵巧操作，可以系垃圾袋之类的东西，并对多指手做非常精细的控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's where my internal model is also updating, right?
zh: 所以我的内在模型也在这里更新，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: All the tasks that the gripper robots could do and that they were at the frontier of dexterity, the hand robots can do now.
zh: 夹爪机器人能做的所有任务，以及它们曾是灵巧性前沿的那些任务，现在手部机器人都能做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the hand robots can do more things that the gripper robots could not do.
zh: 不过也许拧不太紧的罐子不行，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in a way, hands are now at the frontier of dexterity and grippers are maybe not.
zh: 所以从某种意义上说，手部现在处于灵巧性的前沿，而夹爪可能已经不是了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this has been, I think I was quite surprised at how much the hardware has come along.
zh: 我觉得这一点，说实话，硬件进步之大让我相当惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a lot of hands on the market that are quite good, that people are doing a lot of research with.
zh: 市面上有很多相当不错的手，人们正在用它们做大量研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is still more work need to be done about how to make them very reliable, very repeatable, and also make them cheaper.
zh: 不过要让它们变得非常可靠、非常可重复，以及更便宜，还有更多工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: How strong are they?
zh: 它们的力量有多强？

speaker: Unknown
en: If my wife needs me to open a jar, would the robot be able to substitute for me and open the jar for her?
zh: 如果我妻子需要我打开一个罐子，机器人能不能替代我去帮她开罐子？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or would it be like she would need to open jars that the robot can't open?
zh: 还是说她会遇到机器人打不开、需要她自己开的罐子？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like where does it fit on the kind of the, in addition to the dexterity, the ability to really torque something?
zh: 就是说，除了灵巧性之外，它在真正拧动东西的力量方面处于什么位置？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there is a spectrum and it depends on which hands that you use.
zh: 我觉得存在一个区间，取决于你用哪种手。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think especially even off the shelf, there are a lot of variations.
zh: 我觉得尤其是即便都是现成品，也有很多差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: The wuji hand is closer to, I think, maybe like a 10 year old, I would say.
zh: wuji 手更接近，我觉得，大概相当于一个 10 岁孩子的力量，我会这么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bit weaker and the sharper hand is, I think it can lift like 20 kgs.
zh: 它稍弱一些，而 sharper 手，我觉得能举起大概 20 公斤。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how much the torque stuff, but I've seen it open jars, so I'm pretty sure that's possible.
zh: 扭力方面我不清楚多少，但我见过它开罐子，所以我很确定那是可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Though maybe not a very tight one, I don't know.
zh: 虽然可能不是一个很紧的,我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there is a lot of spectrum and some hands are built for lifting more.
zh: 所以区间很大，有些手就是为了更大举重能力而造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The sharper hand is also much bigger than my hand.
zh: sharper 手也比我的手大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the woojee hand is maybe close, more closer and human sized.
zh: 而 woojee 手可能更接近人类尺寸。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'd be funny if the last job for humans is opening stuck jars that the robots don't quite have the wrist strength for.
zh: 如果人类最后一份工作是帮机器人拧开它们手腕力量不足以打开的卡死罐子，那还挺搞笑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Random aside, it's fine if the answer is nothing or it's all fake, but what is soft robotics?
zh: 随便问一句，如果答案是“没什么”或“全是炒作”也没关系，软体机器人是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you know about soft robotics?
zh: 你对软体机器人了解多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: What should I be paying attention to?
zh: 我应该关注些什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I recently talked to a founder in this space, and honestly, I came away more confused than I went into that conversation.
zh: 我最近和这个领域的一位创始人聊过，说实话，聊完比聊之前更困惑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, it was funny.
zh: 基本上，挺有意思的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They basically wouldn't really think.
zh: 他们基本上不太愿意思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, why did you schedule an interview if you don't want to say anything at all about what you're doing?
zh: 我心想，如果你完全不想说你正在做的事情，为什么还要安排这次访谈？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was a random kind of strange experiment or experience, but I did nevertheless come away thinking, what should I be paying attention to, if anything, in soft robotics?
zh: 所以那是一次随机的、有点奇怪的实验或经历，但我还是带着这个问题离开：软体机器人领域，如果有的话，我应该关注什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Regarding soft robotics, there is a wide spectrum.
zh: 关于软体机器人，区间非常宽。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have seen things from people building soft bodies to people building very soft hands.
zh: 我见过从做软体身体的人，到做非常软的手的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's relevant for AI-driven robotics is what's repeatable and what's durable.
zh: 而对 AI 驱动的机器人来说，重要的是什么是可重复的、什么是耐用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One trend that I'm very interested in is like the UMI type of effort for a lot of gloves and stuff and for a lot of like tactile modality.
zh: 有一个趋势我非常感兴趣，就是像 UMI 那类的努力，用于大量手套之类的东西，以及大量触觉模态。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that type of how to do them really well and how to build that really well is still an area of research.
zh: 我觉得如何把它们做得非常好、如何把那一块构建得非常好，仍然是一个研究课题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of it is like soft robotics, I think.
zh: 而其中一部分，我觉得，就是软体机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I'm not, I'm not, I'm also not fully, roboticists are of different kind.
zh: 嗯，我不，我不，我也不完全……机器人学家有好几种。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are also like a lot of roboticists who are like very, like very mechanical engineering focused and then who see the work that I'm doing, you're not a real roboticist.
zh: 也有很多机器人学家非常、非常偏机械工程，他们看到我做的工作会说，你算不上真正的机器人学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, sure, okay.
zh: 然后我说，行吧，好吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Computer science roboticists and the mechanical engineering.
zh: 有计算机科学出身的机器人学家，也有机械工程出身的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, you should go to a robotics conference.
zh: 哦，你应该去一次机器人学会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all kinds of people.
zh: 那里什么人都有。

speaker: Unknown
en: ICRA is a good example.
zh: ICRA 就是个好例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's every kind of roboticist there.
zh: 那里有各种各样类型的机器人学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sounds fun.
zh: 听起来很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did have a chance to go to WAIC in Shanghai this summer, and there were a ton of robots there.
zh: 我今年夏天确实有机会去了上海的 WAIC，那里有海量机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mostly felt like the demos seemed highly staged.
zh: 我总体感觉那些演示看起来高度彩排过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't feel like they were really demonstrating a lot of generalization ability in most of the things that they were showing off.
zh: 我没觉得他们展示的大部分东西真正体现了多少泛化能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like a CES scale show with multiple giant venues and every AI company in China basically there.
zh: 那是一个 CES 规模的展会，有好几个巨型场馆，基本上中国的每家 AI 公司都在。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a cool experience.
zh: 那是一次很酷的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: The funniest robotics, specifically the experience I had there was sitting down at the Tencent booth.
zh: 在那里我和机器人相关最有意思的经历，是坐在腾讯展台。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had a sort of half humanoid.
zh: 他们有一个类似半人形的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it had legs.
zh: 我不觉得它有腿。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was just mounted upper body.
zh: 我觉得它只是被固定住的上半身。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was giving massages.
zh: 然后它在做按摩。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I got a very brief robot massage, some sort of like pressure point thing.
zh: 所以我得到了一次非常简短的机器人按摩,某种类似穴位按压的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was too short to really score.
zh: 时间太短了,没法真正打分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It didn't hurt me.
zh: 它没有弄疼我。

speaker: Unknown
en: It did apply some, like, non-trivial pressure.
zh: 它确实施加了一些,呃,不小的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I walked away with a smile on my face.
zh: 我离开时脸上带着微笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess it wasn't too bad, but I'm not sure.
zh: 我想它还不算太糟,但我不确定。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I still would be highly confident that a human massage would be better.
zh: 我想我仍然会非常有信心地认为人类按摩会更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're letting robots touch people over there now.
zh: 他们现在让机器人碰人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something.
zh: 这算是件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of robots touching people and potentially crossing other lines...
zh: 说到机器人碰人、还可能越过其他界限……

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody, of course, this summer is talking about OpenFace, the scandal, the incident, I can sometimes call it a lab leak out of OpenAI.
zh: 当然了,各位,今年夏天大家都在谈论 OpenFace,那场丑闻,那个事件,我有时会把它称为 OpenAI 的一次实验室泄漏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it just has me thinking, like, maybe the research is all going to work and the alignment and the safety questions will ultimately be the bottleneck on robotics deployments.
zh: 这让我不禁想,也许研究最终都会成功,而对齐和安全问题最终会成为机器人部署的瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could analyze that in multiple ways.
zh: 你可以从多个角度分析这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One way to think about it is just like...
zh: 一种思考方式就是……

speaker: Unknown
en: When do you think if we put the alignment and safety questions aside, I might get my domestic servant robot and then people can think for themselves, oh, I think that's like for or after I would expect alignment to be good enough to actually want one.
zh: 你觉得什么时候——如果我们把对齐和安全问题放在一边——我能得到我的家庭仆人机器人,然后人们可以自己想想,哦,我觉得那是在……之前还是之后,我预期对齐要好到什么程度才会真的想要一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think this is definitely an area that we think very carefully about.
zh: 是的,我认为这绝对是我们非常仔细思考的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think of safety as like a capability, right?
zh: 而且我把安全看作一种能力,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I, there is a lot of discussion around like safety and capabilities being at odds with each other, but people are not going to use an unsafe robot and unsafe agents.
zh: 就像,有很多讨论说安全和能力彼此对立,但人们不会使用不安全的机器人和不安全的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the most
zh: 我认为最

speaker: Unknown
en: Useful agents are going to be ones that are safe, that know what they need to do, and they're not overriding human instructions and causing chaos or breaking laws and stuff.
zh: 有用的智能体会是那些安全的智能体,它们知道自己需要做什么,不会覆盖人类的指令、不会制造混乱或违反法律之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think safety needs to be front and center in the design for AI and also robotics.
zh: 所以我认为安全需要在 AI 以及机器人的设计中处于最核心的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And especially in robotics, like in robotics, though, I think there are different types of safety.
zh: 尤其是在机器人领域,不过,我认为安全有不同的类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe one thing that is not relevant to AI safety is operational safety, right?
zh: 也许有一件事与 AI 安全无关,那就是操作安全,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how do you make sure the robot is not like injuring people?
zh: 比如,你怎么确保机器人不会伤害人?

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is not injuring people because you're malicious, but just...
zh: 而这里说的不是因为你怀有恶意而伤害人,而是……

speaker: Unknown
en: In not injuring people because you're dumb and a humanoid being stable enough, like there it's not doing a wild plot to take over your house, but it's just if it falls, it can still be quite dangerous.
zh: 对应完成:你可以蒙着眼睛继续做任务,但正确的做法应该是真正意识到,嘿,有东西挡住了我的视线。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are like a lot of different safety.
zh: 所以安全有很多不同的种类。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's maybe like one type of safety research that's like very specific to robotics, but not yet.
zh: 那也许是一种非常专门针对机器人的安全研究,但目前还没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't see it being a big thing in the AI space.
zh: 我没看到它在 AI 领域成为一件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then there is also things like
zh: 但还有诸如

speaker: Unknown
en: What should I do if there are like obviously like the higher level goal stuff, right?
zh: 我该怎么做,显然还有更高层目标方面的事情,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like how do you make sure you do the task that the human is asking but without breaking guardrails?
zh: 比如你怎么确保完成人类要求的任务,同时不打破护栏?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there is also the stuff about, and maybe this is also specific to robotics, like what happens like when some sensors go wrong and how should I react in those situations?
zh: 然后还有,也许这也是机器人特有的,比如当某些传感器出问题时会发生什么,在这些情况下我应该如何反应?

speaker: Unknown
en: This one very funny demo that we showed was like the humanoid is doing something and then someone goes in and puts a basket on top of its head.
zh: 我们展示过一个非常好笑的演示,人形机器人正在做某件事,然后有人走过去把一个篮子扣在它头上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now what should you do?
zh: 那现在你该怎么办?

speaker: Unknown
en: You can continue doing the task with your eyes covered, but the right thing to do there would be like really seeing that, hey, like something is obstructing my vision.
zh: 你可以蒙着眼睛继续做这个任务,但正确的做法是真正意识到,嘿,有什么东西挡住了我的视线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I, can you please remove it?
zh: 能不能,你能把它拿开吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think safety and safety is like a full system thing, right?
zh: 所以我认为安全是一个全系统的事情,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it goes all the way from like the design and the mechanical design of the robot system safety to all the way to like the ER and the high level brain.
zh: 它从机器人的设计和机械设计、系统安全,一直贯穿到 ER 和高层大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how I think about it.
zh: 这就是我对它的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think as AI becomes more capable.
zh: 我确实认为随着 AI 变得更强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we need to think, spend more flops thinking about safety.
zh: 比如,我们需要思考,花更多的算力去思考安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, your example of somebody messing with the robot is an interesting one.
zh: 是的,你说的有人捣乱机器人的例子很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we've seen this with Waymos and stuff, obviously, right, where people, like, go out of their way to cause trouble for AI systems.
zh: 我是说,我们在 Waymo 之类的东西上显然见过这种情况,对吧,人们会特意去给 AI 系统制造麻烦。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, it's something that I was very surprised of.
zh: 事实上,这是我非常惊讶的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, maybe because you, and it's hard, right?
zh: 就像,也许因为你,而且这很难,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You have two brains in you.
zh: 你体内有两个大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: One brain is the researcher brain who knows that they are machines.
zh: 一个大脑是研究者大脑，他们知道这些是机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you don't really treat them as human-like.
zh: 所以现在你并不会真的把它们当作像人一样的存在来对待。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then there's the other brain, which is like, because they look so human-like, it's a bit duplicitous, right?
zh: 但还有另一个大脑，就是说，因为它们看起来非常像人，这有点自相矛盾，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when it's talking and stuff, you feel kind of very human-like around them.
zh: 因为当它在说话什么的，你在它旁边会感觉它挺像人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, so as a researcher, I'm like very careful a little bit, but I think when we see new people interacting with robots, they're very...
zh: 所以，作为研究者，我会稍微谨慎一点，但我认为当我们看到新人与机器人互动时，他们非常……

speaker: Unknown
en: People need to be more aware that these are machines.
zh: 人们需要更清楚地意识到这些是机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think sometimes when new people interact with the robots, because it looks very human-like, that boundary can blur.
zh: 而且我认为有时新人接触机器人时，因为它看起来非常像人，那条边界会变得模糊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think this also creates a higher bar for humanoids.
zh: 我还认为这也为人形机器人树立了更高的门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have gripper-based robots, it makes a mistake.
zh: 如果你有一个基于夹爪的机器人，它出了个错。

speaker: Unknown
en: People don't expect it to be smart, but a humanoid just grappling around and creating a lot of failures would be judged much harshly because...
zh: 人们不会指望它聪明，但一个人形机器人在那里乱摸一通、制造很多失败，就会被严厉得多地评判，因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if you say, okay, this is the state of the manipulation research or whatever, people still expect humanoids to act smarter than robots that look anything unlike it.
zh: 即使你说，好吧，这就是操作研究的现状之类的，人们仍然期望人形机器人表现得比任何长得不像人的机器人更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's interesting.
zh: 是的，这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to go down too much of a rabbit hole on consciousness, but...
zh: 我不想在意识这个问题上钻得太深，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think it's incredibly striking to me over the last year how much analogous structure has been found in LOMs.
zh: 我确实认为，在过去一年里，LOM 中发现了多少类似的结构，这一点让我非常震撼。
